The relevant oxygen-reduction couples are

\[
\ce{O2 + 4H+ + 4e- -> 2H2O}\qquad E^\circ=+1.229\ \text{V}
\]

and

\[
\ce{O2 + 2H2O + 4e- -> 4OH-}\qquad E^\circ=+0.401\ \text{V}.
\]

The lower reduction potential in basic solution means that \(\ce{O2}\) is thermodynamically a **weaker** oxidant there.

Although electrode potentials do not determine rates, oxygen reduction is conventionally observed to be kinetically more facile in alkaline media for many aqueous and electrocatalytic systems. Thus, under the usual comparison intended by the question, \(\ce{O2}\) reacts **more slowly in acidic solutions**. Strictly, the kinetic ordering can depend on the catalyst and reductant.

Answer: B
